title: Finite-graph diffusion eigenfunction extrapolation
formal_object: Positive symmetric training-anchor kernel K, degree D=diag(K1), reversible P=D^-1K and S=D^-1/2 K D^-1/2; nonstationary eigenpairs (lambda,u).
assumptions: All degrees are positive; retain only stable positive nonzero eigenvalues and remove the stationary direction.
Anchors/statistics/coordinates come only from train; no test graph or label selection.
Finite graph coordinates do not imply continuum semantic consistency; dot-product scoring is not automatically diffusion distance.

operations.condition: lambda nonzero and training graph fixed

derivation_steps.justification: Direct multiplication identifies the reversible-chain eigenfunction rather than calling u itself a Markov eigenfunction.
The eigen-equation supplies the 1/lambda factor. This justifies the legacy time-minus-one weight.

derivation_steps.statement: Dot products of the extended coordinates omit the per-point squared norms in negative squared diffusion-coordinate distance.
derivation_steps.justification: Expanding -||z(x)-z(y)||^2 gives 2 z(x)z(y)-||z(x)||^2-||z(y)||^2; stationary weighting also matters for diffusion distance.

method_expression: Build a fixed training graph and output its extended coordinates for every native query/candidate; declare coordinate dot-product scoring as the actual method, without naming it a diffusion-distance ranking.
distinguishing_prediction: Coordinate extrapolation changes rankings only when finite graph neighborhoods carry stable useful structure; near-zero lambda and domain shift create an identifiable failure boundary.
falsifier: Matched exact dot/RBF/Nystrom or the corresponding actual diffusion-distance scorer explains equal benefit; graph perturbations destabilize ranking.
closest_alternative: Finite diffusion maps and Nystrom extension; density-dependent continuum results require assumptions absent here.
decisive_comparison: Same anchors/width/output dimension and complete native rankings, including graph fit, extension, serialization and scorer costs; compare score semantics explicitly.
legacy_code_audit: Legacy map uses phi*lambda^(t-1) and train-only anchors correctly; its scoring is a feature dot product, not the spectral diffusion distance.
review_limit: Finite algebra/declared scoring reviewed; continuum theorem, superiority and originality not established.
